name: Fortinet
evidence_summary: Official sources position Fortinet Secure SD-WAN as converged networking/security and FortiSASE as cloud-delivered SSE/SASE.
cost_model: Quote-based appliances/subscriptions/support; public reseller pricing exists for hardware but enterprise managed/SASE bundles require quote.
key_differentiators: Native convergence of networking and security on a single operating system (FortiOS) across FortiGate edge, FortiManager and FortiSASE.
Strong story for buyers who want secure SD-WAN and SASE delivered from one vendor platform rather than assembled from partner integrations.
Wide appliance range covering everything from small branch to large data centre, with public hardware pricing visible through resellers.
best_fit_for: Security-first buyers who want SD-WAN and SASE under a single policy and log domain.
Mid-market and enterprise organisations that already run FortiGate firewalls and want to extend into SD-WAN and cloud-delivered security.
Buyers comparing single-vendor SASE platforms (alongside Cato, Palo Alto, Cisco) for converged operations.
watch_outs: Like Cisco, managed delivery is via partners rather than Fortinet directly; underlay and field operations are not owned by the vendor.
Buyers wanting a private global backbone will need to validate FortiSASE PoP coverage against their geographic footprint.
Best-of-breed buyers may prefer integrating FortiGate SD-WAN with a separate SSE platform (Zscaler, Netskope) rather than adopting full FortiSASE.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Industry, region, organisation-size and pricing evidence was sourced on the same basis. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason. The value_tier field is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim: most of this market publishes no price. Sources found and rejected are listed at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: FortiAI assistant, FortiAIOps and FortiGuard AI-powered security services.

resilience.note: HA clustering, multi-hub designs and FortiSASE regional PoPs.

profile.platform_architecture: Fortinet builds SD-WAN into FortiGate, so every firewall is also an SD-WAN edge. Path selection, application steering and overlay VPN run on FortiOS with orchestration through FortiManager and analytics through FortiAnalyzer. Custom ASICs give strong price-to-performance, particularly for encrypted traffic at branch scale. Cloud on-ramps cover AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud, and edge form factors run from desktop units to chassis.
profile.security_sase: Security is the heritage: NGFW, IPS, web filtering, sandboxing and SSL inspection are native on the same appliance, backed by FortiGuard threat intelligence. FortiSASE extends the stack to cloud-delivered SWG, ZTNA, CASB and DLP from Fortinet PoPs, with universal ZTNA spanning on-premises and cloud enforcement. For buyers wanting one OS across branch firewalling and SASE, the convergence is among the tightest available.
profile.service_support_channel: Fortinet is channel-led with deep UK distribution and MSP support, and is the platform behind many managed offers, including BT Managed SASE on Fortinet. FortiCare provides 24x7 support tiers with professional services for migration. DIY, co-managed and fully managed routes are all realistic, and multi-tenant tooling makes it a favourite among MSPs.
profile.commercials_verdict: Commercials bundle hardware with FortiCare support and FortiGuard security subscriptions; FortiSASE adds per-user licensing. Pricing is quote based but consistently aggressive against like-for-like NGFW plus SD-WAN stacks. The Netify verdict: shortlist Fortinet when security and WAN budgets are one budget, when branch performance per pound matters, or when an existing FortiGate estate makes convergence the path of least resistance.

vendor_faqs.q: Is Fortinet SD-WAN really free with the firewall?
vendor_faqs.a: SD-WAN features ship in FortiOS on every FortiGate, so there is no separate SD-WAN licence. You still pay for FortiCare support and FortiGuard security bundles, and FortiSASE per-user licences if you add the cloud security layer.

vendor_faqs.q: How strong is FortiSASE against cloud-native rivals?
vendor_faqs.a: FortiSASE delivers ZTNA, SWG, CASB and DLP from Fortinet PoPs with one policy language across appliance and cloud. Cloud-native rivals carry larger PoP fabrics; Fortinet counters with FortiGate integration and total cost. Test from your user geographies before deciding.

vendor_faqs.q: Can I get Fortinet as a managed service in the UK?
vendor_faqs.a: Yes. BT, Vodafone and many UK MSPs offer managed Fortinet SD-WAN and SASE, including co-managed models where your team keeps policy visibility while the provider runs lifecycle and incident response.

shortlist_summary: Fortinet run FortiOS across FortiGate edge, FortiManager and FortiSASE, meaning networking and security policy are converged on a single operating system rather than integrated via API across separate components. Typically shortlisted by organisations already standardised on Fortinet hardware at the edge, or those looking for a vendor where the convergence story is backed up by a common OS rather than a marketing claim.
cost_note: Strong price-to-performance from custom ASICs; SD-WAN ships in FortiOS so there is no separate SD-WAN licence.
uk_basis: No UK HQ (US). Strong UK channel and FortiSASE PoPs; widely delivered as a UK managed service by BT, Vodafone and UK MSPs.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: Ensure FortiGates, FortiAPs, FortiSwitches and FortiExtenders are quickly and correctly deployed, configured to best practices
f01_fully_managed_service.note: Fortinet itself operates Managed FortiGate Service (MFGS), in which Fortinet NOC staff carry out deployment, configuration, provisioning and ongoing change management. The solution page adds "Deployment, configuration, provisioning, and regular changes" and "Evaluate, implement, and verify configuration changes". Note that this is a managed wrap around Fortinet's own appliances rather than an end-to-end managed WAN including circuits; most fully managed Fortinet SD-WAN in the market is delivered by carrier and MSSP partners rather than by Fortinet.

f03_co_managed_service.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. I read the Managed FortiGate Service datasheet and solution page, the FortiSASE Unified SASE for MSSP multitenancy guide and the G-Cloud service definition. None of them states a shared responsibility or co-management split in which the customer retains named policy and change rights. The MSSP guide describes Read-Only and Read-Write permission profiles, but that governs MSSP staff scope rather than a customer or provider co-management contract, so it is not sufficient.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.quote: The portal offers centralized multi-tenant management and configuration capabilities, enabling MSSPs to efficiently deploy and manage SASE services across their client base.
f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: Tenant isolation and delegated administration are evidenced: the FortiSASE datasheet describes an MSSP Portal, and the service provider page states "Fortinet solutions are multi-tenant from the ground up, enabling MSPs and MSSPs to isolate and manage multiple customer networks from a single administrative console." Graded partial rather than yes because no page reviewed evidences branded or white-label portals for the MSP's own brand, and because the FortiSASE MSSP architecture guide qualifies the model by saying each customer gets a separate isolated instance. See conflicts.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: A series of workshops, along with Q&A sessions, will be scheduled to provide the education necessary to implement the solution.
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: Fortinet Professional Services lists named offerings including a FortiGate SD-WAN QuickStart Service, a FortiSASE Advanced Deployment Service, Design Workshop Service, Configuration Review Service, Upgrade Plan Service and "Firewall Migration and Replacement Project" for customers migrating from third-party vendors. Discovery, phased deployment and training are covered. Explicit rollback plans were not found on the pages reviewed.

f07_lifecycle_management.quote: Let MFGS experts handle your firmware upgrades to maximize effectiveness and minimize risk
f07_lifecycle_management.note: Firmware upgrade and patching are handled as part of Managed FortiGate Service, which also states "Automatically trigger patching for vulnerabilities with a severity rating of medium or higher". The FortiCare support page covers hardware replacement ("Meet your availability requirements with our Priority RMA Services.") and describes "comprehensive lifecycle services". Explicit end-of-life planning and renewals handling as part of the service were not found.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: FortiExtender cellular gateways and routers provide secure 5G/LTE connectivity for any deployment.
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: FortiExtender is Fortinet's own product line. The page also states "Easily provision 5G or LTE wireless WAN, high availability, and failover, as well as out-of-band management (OOB) and private 5G/LTE." and "FortiExtender 5G/LTE Wireless WAN gateways come equipped with Dual SIM and Dual Modem capabilities for fast failover and active/active cellular connectivity." covering dual SIM and both primary and failover transport. Signal quality is addressed by "FortiExtender cellular gateways and routers ensure optimal signal reception, minimal attenuation, and the best experience."

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: Our global SASE network spans 170+ PoPs, providing low-latency, high-performance connectivity.
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: Graded yes because these are Fortinet's own FortiSASE PoPs running Fortinet's own security stack, not a third party's gateways resold by Fortinet. The datasheet adds "Fortinet delivers 99.999% SLA with latency guarantee for security inspection, which is possible because of global reach with hundreds of security PoPs." Fortinet does host part of the footprint on hyperscaler infrastructure, per the Google Cloud press release statement "The partnership allows Fortinet to leverage Google Cloud's global network edge locations closest to their regions of presence", and the FortiSASE page itself concedes "Part of this network is owned by Fortinet, ensuring greater control, reliability, and security." The service layer remains Fortinet's.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. A FortiSASE Sovereign administration guide and architecture guide exist in Fortinet's document library and their titles imply dedicated or sovereign deployment, but the PDFs returned HTTP 403 in this session so I could not read them and will not grade from a search result title. A "Dedicated public IP addresses" documentation page was also surfaced but not read. The FortiSASE product page reviewed describes only the shared multi-tenant PoP network. This should be re-checked once the Sovereign guides are retrievable.

f21_private_global_backbone.quote: Part of this network is owned by Fortinet, ensuring greater control, reliability, and security.
f21_private_global_backbone.note: Graded partial, not yes. The word "backbone" does not appear anywhere on the FortiSASE product page. Fortinet claims ownership only of part of the PoP network, and the Google Cloud press release confirms that a portion of the footprint rides Google Cloud's network edge rather than a Fortinet-owned inter-region backbone. No source reviewed makes a claim about vendor-owned or vendor-controlled transit between regions with committed latency and loss.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: Fortinet delivers 99.999% SLA with latency guarantee for security inspection, which is possible because of global reach with hundreds of security PoPs.
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: Contractual rather than best-effort. Fortinet's own G-Cloud 14 FortiSASE service definition sets out availability tiers (Management Portal 99.99%, Individual Security POPs 99.99%, Overall service in high availability configuration 99.999%) and commits that "FortiSASE cloud platform is managed by Fortinet on a twenty-four (24) hours a day by seven (7) days a week basis and is monitored for hardware availability, service capacity, and network resource utilization." Support response commitments come via "24 x 7 FortiCare Technical Support". A latency commitment is claimed alongside uptime. Change handling commitments were not found in the SLA text reviewed.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.quote: Secure SD-WAN, SSE, zero trust, wireless controller, LTE/5G gateway, and FortiGuard AI-Powered Security Services have the same OS, policy engine, and management plane.
f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: Native, not partner_integrated. Fortinet authors FortiOS and the FortiGate NGFW itself, and the SD-WAN function is a feature of the same operating system rather than a bolt-on appliance. The FortiSASE datasheet confirms the cloud-delivered equivalent: "FortiSASE FWaaS is a cloud-based service that provides hyperscale, next-generation firewall (NGFW) capabilities, including web filtering, advanced threat protection (ATP), intrusion prevention system (IPS), and Domain Name System (DNS) security." Stateful firewalling, application control, IPS, malware inspection and URL filtering are all in-platform.

f33_data_loss_prevention.quote: The FortiSASE DLP feature supports advanced data matching techniques, including pattern recognition and contextual analysis, to effectively prevent accidental data breaches.
f33_data_loss_prevention.note: Native Fortinet capability. The FortiSASE datasheet adds "Identify, monitor, and protect organization data at rest and in motion. DLP engine backed by FortiGuard AI feeds with over thousands of pre-defined data patterns, updated to protect from day zero." and "DLP allows businesses to identify sensitive information across multiple cloud-based systems, prevent the accidental sharing of data, and monitor and protect data." Classification, inspection and blocking are evidenced. Alerting workflows and formal exception or override workflows were not found on the pages reviewed.

delivery_model.quote: FortiSASE cloud platform is managed by Fortinet on a twenty-four (24) hours a day by seven (7) days a week basis and is monitored for hardware availability, service capacity, and network resource utilization.
delivery_model.note: Fortinet is primarily a technology vendor that authors its own products (FortiOS, FortiGate, FortiExtender, FortiManager) and sells them to enterprises and to carriers and MSSPs who wrap their own managed services around them. It is also a managed provider in its own right for specific services: it operates the FortiSASE cloud platform and PoP network, and it sells Managed FortiGate Service delivered by its own NOC. The bulk of managed Fortinet SD-WAN in the UK and global market, however, is operated by partners such as those named on the service provider page rather than by Fortinet directly.

underlay_ownership.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. I checked the SD-WAN product page, the FortiSASE product page, the FortiExtender page, the service provider managed SD-WAN page and the G-Cloud service definition; none states whether Fortinet owns physical circuits or core routing. The available signals point in opposite directions and neither is decisive: the FortiSASE page claims "Part of this network is owned by Fortinet, ensuring greater control, reliability, and security." while the Google Cloud press release shows part of the footprint riding a hyperscaler's network edge. Both statements concern the PoP and cloud network rather than access circuits. My working expectation is that Fortinet sells software and appliances over customer-procured or partner-procured transport, which would make this customer_supplied_only, but I found no quote establishing that and will not grade from prior knowledge.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Secure SD-WAN, SSE, zero trust, wireless controller, LTE/5G gateway, and FortiGuard AI-Powered Security Services have the same OS, policy engine, and management plane.
sse_layer_ownership.note: Fortinet built its own SSE stack. Secure web gateway, firewall as a service, zero trust access and DLP all run on FortiOS and FortiGuard, which Fortinet authors, and are delivered from Fortinet's own FortiSASE PoPs. There is no third-party security vendor in the path. This is the reference case for the opposite direction of the test: carriers such as BT that resell managed Fortinet SASE are graded partner with note Fortinet, whereas Fortinet itself is native. The only qualification is infrastructure hosting, since some PoPs sit on Google Cloud edge locations, but the security software and enforcement layer are Fortinet's own.

regulatory_documentation.note: Fortinet's product certifications page names specific frameworks rather than making a general assurance statement, which meets the documented threshold. Frameworks found named on that page: ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, FIPS 140-2 and 140-3, Common Criteria, HIPAA, CSA STAR, TISAX, ISMAP, DoDIN APL, NSA CSfC, TAA and Section 508. Frameworks NOT found on any page reviewed: NHS DSPT, DORA, NIS2. Caveat on confidence: the page is an index, so the named certifications are not tied there to a specific product scope or to a retrievable attestation report, and the G-Cloud service definition reviewed did not mention ISO 27001 or SOC 2 at all.

pop_count.quote: Our global SASE network spans 170+ PoPs, providing low-latency, high-performance connectivity.
pop_count.note: Taken from the FortiSASE product page FAQ and re-verified as literally present with a second targeted fetch. Confidence is medium rather than high because the FortiSASE datasheet instead says "hundreds of security PoPs", which is a looser and arguably larger figure, and because the product page is undated so the number cannot be pinned to a release. Both figures are vendor self-reported with no third-party audit found. Recorded in conflicts.

sla_availability_pct.quote: Fortinet delivers 99.999% SLA with latency guarantee for security inspection, which is possible because of global reach with hundreds of security PoPs.
sla_availability_pct.note: The 99.999 headline figure is qualified in Fortinet's own G-Cloud service definition, which breaks availability down as Management Portal 99.99%, Individual Security POPs 99.99%, and Overall service (in high availability configuration) 99.999%. So five nines applies only where the customer buys a high availability configuration; a single PoP carries four nines. The FortiSASE product page also hedges, saying uptime is "typically offering 99.999% uptime". Buyers should read the figure as conditional. Recorded in conflicts.

sectors.healthcare.quote: The healthcare industry is undergoing digital transformation with the adoption of Internet-of-Medical-Things (IoMT) devices and digital technology, expanding the attack surface.
sectors.healthcare.note: Dedicated healthcare industry page. Re-fetch confirmed the exact strings "Halifax Health", "Heartland Dental" and "Atrius Health" all appear verbatim on the same page as named customers, alongside RWJBarnabas Health, Enzo Biochem and Mater Health North Queensland. The SD-WAN customer stories ebook [9] additionally carries an anonymised "Largest Dental Services" provider with 700+ locations, which is SD-WAN-specific rather than generic security. Grade rests on named customers plus a dedicated page, not on inference.

sectors.financial_services.quote: The financial services sector is a high-value target for cyberattacks and highly regulated by jurisdictions around the world.
sectors.financial_services.note: Dedicated financial services industry page. USI Insurance Services is named and quoted on that page saying "Secure SD-WAN does what it is supposed to do." The SD-WAN customer stories ebook [9] names Itau Unibanco with 3,000+ locations across 20 countries, which is direct SD-WAN evidence. Other financial customers on the page are anonymised by descriptor (a Vietnamese bank, a US multinational institution).

sectors.retail_ecommerce.quote: With the Fortinet Secure SD-WAN solution in place, those stores stayed online. In fact, they were not even aware of the outage.
sectors.retail_ecommerce.note: Strongest sector evidence in the set: The Paper Store is named on the dedicated retail page and quoted about Secure SD-WAN specifically, not generic security. Bozzuto's, Cub, Fat Brands, Checkers Drive-In Restaurants and Batteries Plus Bulbs are also named and quoted on the same page. Supertiendas Olimpica appears via the SD-WAN product page.

sectors.manufacturing.quote: Our extended IT infrastructure is absolutely critical to everything we do, so it's invaluable to have the seamless protection that Fortinet provides across our physical and cloud-based domains.
sectors.manufacturing.note: Quote attributed to Steelcase on the dedicated manufacturing page. GEMU, Kalsec, Barnes Group and Toyota Material Handling are also named on that page. The SD-WAN ebook [9] carries a global auto parts company (~11,000 locations, 17 countries) and a bakery manufacturer (1,000 locations, 32 countries) as SD-WAN deployments. Note the Steelcase quote evidences platform security rather than SD-WAN specifically; the SD-WAN link comes from [9].

sectors.energy_utilities.quote: Fortinet solutions are user friendly and easy to configure and deploy.
sectors.energy_utilities.note: Quote attributed to Elektroprivreda BiH on the dedicated Power and Utilities page; chosen over the longer ENGIE Italia pull-quote because short testimonial strings verify more reliably. Echoenergia, Falu Energi & Vatten, Houston County Electric Cooperative and ENGIE Italia are also named on that page, and it hosts a NERC CIP deployment paper. Fortinet also runs separate dedicated Oil and Gas and SCADA/ICS pages [16], and the SD-WAN ebook [9] includes a global oil and gas company with 400+ locations. Plains All American Pipeline and ExxonMobil appear on the customers index [2].

sectors.government_public_sector.quote: Fortinet solutions meet government compliance requirements such as FISMA, NIST, and CJIS
sectors.government_public_sector.note: Dedicated State and Local Government page plus a separate Federal Government page [16]. Named public sector customers on the page include City of Portland, Illinois Century Network, Felgueiras City Council and Hornsby Shire Council; Schenectady County appears on the customers index [2]. Compliance framework claim supports the grade. Caveat: this evidence is general Fortinet security rather than SD-WAN specifically, and I did not find a named government SD-WAN deployment.

sectors.education.quote: We did not experience any difference at all from the pre-sale to post-sale support, which speaks volumes about Fortinet's commitment to its customers.
sectors.education.note: Quote attributed to Dr. Mehran Basiratmand, Executive Director and CTO, Florida Atlantic University, on the dedicated Higher Education page. Wageningen University & Research, Anahuac University Network, Northeast Texas Community College and ITAM are also named and quoted there. Separate dedicated K-12 School Districts page exists [16]. Coomera Anglican College and St. Andrews Lutheran College appear on the customers index [2]. Worth noting the general /industries/education page [7] carries no named institutions at all, so the evidence sits on the higher-ed page.

sectors.transport_logistics.quote: With all those benefits and advantages over the previous managed WAN, perhaps the most astonishing result is the significant reduction in overall cost.
sectors.transport_logistics.note: Quote attributed to Kevin Rowland, Chief Information Officer, Fliway, one of New Zealand's largest integrated logistics providers, in a case study explicitly about replacing a managed WAN with Fortinet Secure SD-WAN across 13 branches and 6 warehouses. Confidence is medium rather than high because the dedicated Transportation industry page [19] itself carries no named customers, so the grade rests on a single named case study. Waste Management also surfaced as a case study URL in search but I did not read that page, so it is not cited.

sectors.professional_services.note: Honest unknown. I checked: the industries index [16] lists sixteen dedicated industry pages and none is professional services, consulting, legal or accounting. The customers index carries a "Business Services" filter label (quoted above, verbatim from the filter taxonomy) but the filtered view did not resolve any named professional services customer. A targeted search for a Fortinet law firm or consulting SD-WAN case study returned only Fortinet's own Professional Services support offering, which is a Fortinet service line and not a customer sector. No sector-specific customer, case study or accreditation found, so no grade is awarded.

sectors.hospitality_leisure.quote: We have reservations coming in through the internet, through third party travel agencies, as well as local traffic.
sectors.hospitality_leisure.note: Quote attributed to Harold Dibler, Vice President of Technology, Best Western Hotels and Resorts, on the dedicated Hospitality page. IHG Hotels & Resorts appears on the customers index [2] with a Secure SD-WAN deployment, and the SD-WAN ebook [9] leads with a global hospitality company at 4,000+ locations and 325,000+ employees. Majestic Resorts is cited on the SD-WAN product page [1]. Note the Best Western quote itself is about reservations security, not SD-WAN; the SD-WAN link comes from [2] and [9].

regions.uk_ireland.note: Taken from the FortiSASE global data centre table in Fortinet's technical documentation, which lists PoPs by city and country rather than sales offices. Three London PoPs are listed (LON-F4 on Fortinet's own cloud, plus LON-G2 and LON-O1 on public cloud). A separate Ireland entry (DUB-A2) also appears; the exact string "Ireland" was verified present, though that row is labelled by country only rather than by city. Exact string forms confirmed on a dedicated re-fetch.

regions.europe.note: Dense European coverage in the FortiSASE PoP table: France (Paris, Valbonne), Germany (Frankfurt), Spain (Madrid), Italy (Milan), Netherlands (Amsterdam), Belgium, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Switzerland and Turkey. Verification caveat worth recording: the exact string "Frankfurt (Germany)" is NOT present; the page renders it as "Frankfurt (German)", which appears to be a typo in Fortinet's own documentation. I have therefore quoted the Paris row, which verified exactly.

regions.north_america.note: Heaviest concentration of PoPs of any region: roughly a dozen US locations (Ashburn, Dallas, Plano, Miami, San Jose, Chicago, Columbus, Las Vegas, Moncks Corner, Portland), four Canadian metros (Burnaby, Toronto, Ottawa, Montreal) and Queretaro in Mexico. Note the US rows use a city-plus-state format, so the exact string is "Ashburn, Virginia (United States)" and not "Ashburn (United States)"; this was confirmed on re-fetch.

regions.asia_pacific.note: Broad APAC coverage in the PoP table: Australia (Sydney, Melbourne, Perth), New Zealand (Auckland), Japan (Tokyo, Osaka, Komagome), Singapore, Hong Kong, India (Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore, Pune), South Korea (Seoul), Taiwan (Taipei), Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines and Malaysia. Note the Singapore row renders as "Singapore (Republic of Singapore)", not bare "Singapore".

regions.middle_east_africa.note: Middle East coverage is strong: UAE (Dubai has four PoPs including two on Fortinet's own cloud, plus Abu Dhabi), Saudi Arabia (Dammam, Jeddah), Qatar (Doha), Oman (Muscat) and Israel (Tel Aviv). African coverage is much thinner and effectively single-country: only Johannesburg (South Africa) appears, verified verbatim as "Johannesburg (South Africa)". Buyers needing West or East African delivery should treat this as unproven.

regions.latin_america.note: PoPs listed in Brazil (Sao Paulo, Vinhedo), Chile (Santiago), Colombia (Bogota), Peru (Lima), Argentina (Buenos Aires) and Mexico (Queretaro). Recording a rendering conflict rather than resolving it: the Fortinet-cloud row verified verbatim as "Sao Paulo (Brazil)" without a diacritic, while the public-cloud row for the same city appears as "Sao Paulo (Brazil)" with an accented a. I have quoted the unaccented form, which was explicitly confirmed present.

regions.china_mainland.note: Deliberate unknown, and the evidence is unusually clean for it. A direct re-fetch of the FortiSASE global data centre table confirmed that no mainland Chinese city (Beijing, Shanghai or Shenzhen) appears anywhere on the page. The only nearby entries are Hong Kong (HKG-F1, HKG-G2) and Taipei (TPE-G2), quoted above, neither of which constitutes mainland delivery. Fortinet does publish a Mainland China simplified-Chinese locale on its website [1], but per method a website language is explicitly not evidence of service delivery, and the same applies to any generic global claim. Mainland China delivery would require a separately licensed arrangement that I found no evidence of.

organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.quote: Fortinet secures the largest enterprise, service provider, and government organizations around the world.
organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.note: Explicit vendor targeting statement, backed by scale evidence rather than assertion alone. The SD-WAN customer stories ebook [9] profiles deployments at Fortune 500 scale: a hospitality group at 4,000+ locations, 325,000+ employees and $19.4 billion revenue; a waste provider at 1,200+ locations described as a "Fortune 500 large enterprise"; Itau Unibanco at 3,000+ locations across 20 countries; and a claims manager operating in 70 countries. These are SD-WAN references specifically.

organisation_fit.mid_market.quote: Small and midsize businesses (SMBs) and managed security service providers (MSSPs) supporting SMB customers need a simple management tool to deploy, manage, and operate network security.
organisation_fit.mid_market.note: Fortinet runs a dedicated SMB solutions page and treats small and midsize as a single addressed segment, so mid-market and small business share the same evidence base. The SD-WAN product page [1] also surfaces a distinct "Small & Midsize Business" navigation entry alongside "Enterprise", indicating separate product routing rather than a single enterprise-only motion. The page does not publish employee or revenue thresholds, so the boundary between mid-market and small business is not defined by the supplier.

organisation_fit.small_business.quote: Fortinet delivers affordable, enterprise-grade security and networking in one easy-to-manage solution, tailored to the needs of SMBs.
organisation_fit.small_business.note: Explicit small business targeting with affordability positioning, on a dedicated SMB page. Supporting language on the same page includes "Get purpose-built security with the best price-per-performance, reducing costs and resource needs." Caveat for buyers: this is a whole-portfolio SMB claim covering security and networking generally, and I found no small business SD-WAN case study or published SMB SD-WAN price point, so the targeting is proven but SMB SD-WAN delivery is not separately evidenced.

published_pricing.quote: Easily transition to FortiSASE security service edge (SSE) with simplified licensing, also delivering lower costs; about one-third of competitor offerings.
published_pricing.note: Fortinet publishes no list price for Secure SD-WAN, so this is graded on positioning language plus one transactable marketplace listing. The quoted claim is an explicit undercut-the-competition statement (roughly a third of rivals' cost). The same page adds "Fortinet Secure SD-WAN has a predictable cost model with no bandwidth licensing or data transfer charges or services tiering." The SMB page [13] reinforces this with "affordable" and "best price-per-performance". AWS Marketplace [17] gives the only hard published figures found, but for the FortiGate VM firewall SKU rather than an SD-WAN or SASE subscription, with rates from about $0.36 to $5.16 per hour by instance type and a 365-day contract option; it is indicative only. Confidence is medium, not high, because every figure is either vendor self-positioning or an adjacent SKU. Not graded budget: Fortinet positions on price-performance and low TCO against enterprise competitors, not as a cheap product. Buyers should expect appliance plus subscription pricing negotiated through partners, which is why no public entry point exists.
